Normalized (ex-one-off) TTM FCF below $1.0B.

HST.thesis_one_line: Host owns top hotels with beating forecasts, an improved credit rating, and fair pricing, but next year's comparisons will be tougher.
kill_criteria: Comparable hotel RevPAR growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters (the core, most-watched KPI).
Adjusted FFO/share guidance is cut (not just raised more slowly) at any quarterly release -- a genuine reversal, not merely deceleration.
Net debt/EBITDAre rises above ~4.0x (current: 2.95x net debt/EBITDA on ratios.py) without an offsetting asset-sale plan.
The regular quarterly dividend ($0.20/share) is cut.

valuation_consistency.reconciliation: Dossier says HST trades in line with lodging-REIT peers (10.4x FY26 AFFO), not at a premium; that is not a contradiction of V1's 'attractive' call (29th-percentile own-history multiple, +6.2%/yr base case) -- both agree the stock is not overvalued, they just use different reference points (peer-relative vs own-history).

JBHT.thesis_one_line: J.B. Hunt is a strong, low-debt trucking company, but its stock price assumes a brief freight rebound continues, while two of five business lines struggle.
kill_criteria: Intermodal revenue growth (ex-fuel) decelerates back below ~5% YoY for two consecutive quarters -- the core recovery thesis fails.
Truckload (JBT) segment operating losses persist for more than two more quarters without a clear path to breakeven from pricing actions.
Net debt/EBITDA rises above 2.0x (would indicate the buyback/capex-cut strategy has outrun cash generation).
OCF conversion (OCF/NI) stays below 1.0x for two consecutive quarters, signaling the working-capital drag is structural rather than transitory.
Any loss of the 'record' DCS sales pipeline translating to signed, revenue-generating fleet growth within the stated 12-18 month cycle.

valuation_consistency.reconciliation: V1 rates JBHT 'fair' with a positive +6.4%/yr base case (implying ~$266 in 3 years vs $225.46 spot), but the dossier's own probability-weighted scenario centers on $155/share, about 31% below spot, and calls today's multiple 'the rich end' of its own history. Appended a reconciliation paragraph to the dossier's Section 7 explaining the gap and why the dossier's more cautious view is better supported.
